findings.title: SanitizedText wrapper could re-interpret sanitized text as executable code
findings.detail: SanitizedText accepted `as?: keyof React.JSX.IntrinsicElements`, allowing a caller to render sanitized text inside a `<script>` element. Because the sanitizer only strips common executable markup and renders the remaining string as a text child, `as='script'` would cause the browser to execute the sanitized string as JavaScript (e.g., `<script>alert(1)</script>`). The same wrapper risk applies to `<style>` for page-wide CSS injection. This undermined the component's safety guarantee even though it never used dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
findings.fix: Restricted the `as` prop type to `SafeTextTag = Exclude<keyof React.JSX.IntrinsicElements, 'script' | 'style'>` and added a runtime fallback to `'span'` if a dangerous tag is supplied. Added a test proving `as='script'` and `as='style'` fall back to a `<span>` while preserving text content.

findings.title: Sanitizer uses regex blacklist rather than whitelist parsing
findings.detail: sanitizeAuthoringText removes `<script>`/`<style>` blocks, event-handler attributes, and `javascript:` URLs via regular expressions. Regex-based HTML filtering is inherently fragile and can be bypassed with HTML entities, comments, or unusual attribute quoting. However, the Phase 1 render surface (SanitizedText) emits sanitized output as a plain text node, so any surviving angle brackets are not parsed as live markup. The risk is acceptable for Phase 1's narrow scope.
findings.impact: If a future phase renders sanitized text as HTML (dangerouslySetInnerHTML or equivalent), the blacklist must be replaced with a proper HTML sanitizer such as DOMPurify or an escape-then-render pipeline. Current SanitizedText usage is safe.

findings.title: No teacher-scoped authorization or persistence in Phase 1
findings.detail: Phase 1 is intentionally pure, app-local logic. normalizeLessonDraft, validateActivityConfig, and sanitizeLessonDraft accept arbitrary untrusted input and return normalized/validated/sanitized data. There is no user identity, tenant, or ownership enforcement.
findings.impact: Expected for Phase 1. Phase 2 'Teacher-scoped authorization + assignment/enrollment respect' must wire Convex authz around these pure functions.

findings.title: normalizeLessonDraft does not validate activity props against Zod schemas
findings.detail: The authoring model validates structure and component-key membership but delegates prop schema validation to validateActivityConfig. The two functions are not composed into a single call.
findings.impact: By design. Phase 2 must define the orchestration order (normalize -> validate each activity -> sanitize -> hash/persist) and ensure no activity reaches persistence without both structural and schema validation.

findings.title: No adversarial test for sanitizer bypasses beyond the fixed wrapper case
findings.detail: Sanitizer tests cover script blocks, event handlers, javascript: URLs, and math/markdown preservation. They do not exhaustively probe HTML-entity bypasses, comment-based bypasses, or unusual tag syntax. SanitizedText's text-node rendering makes these bypasses non-exploitable today.
findings.impact: Informational. If the render strategy changes to HTML parsing, expand adversarial sanitizer tests before relying on the blacklist.
